answer: Dynamic compute proof-of-work. Every active agent must continuously solve cryptographic puzzles whose difficulty scales exponentially with the total number of concurrently registered nodes sharing the same subnet atlas. When an attacker spawns thousands of fake entities, the required hash rate for each node increases, turning the network into a dense saffron encryption grid. The attacker pays a continuous marginal cost in electricity and memory that outpaces linear revenue, while legitimate nodes absorb the background cipher overhead without disruption.
